title: Blinkit Store Expansion vs. Store-Level Throughput Maturation
research_question: Is Blinkit's scale expansion accompanied by improved store-level throughput?
exact_source_pages: Eternal Q1FY25 Shareholder Letter p.12; Q2FY27 Shareholder Letter p.13
derived_calculations: Throughput per store-day = NOV * 10^7 / (Period-End Stores * 91.25). In Q1 FY25, Blinkit Net Order Value (NOV) was ₹4,061.0 Cr across 639 period-end dark stores, yielding an average throughput of ₹696,465 (~₹6.96 lakh) per store-day. By Q2 FY27, dark stores quadrupled (+322.5% to 2,700 stores) while NOV expanded to ₹20,940.0 Cr (+415.6%), driving average throughput up to ₹849,924 (~₹8.50 lakh) per store-day (+22.0% throughput expansion). [AUDIT NOTE: Prior preliminary drafts erroneously plugged in Swiggy Instamart's GOV of ₹2,724 Cr and ₹9,230 Cr into Blinkit's throughput formula, generating a spurious -20% contraction. Using Blinkit's true disclosed NOV demonstrates robust +22.0% throughput expansion despite massive store footprint scaling].
supporting_evidence: [REPORTED FACT] Store count increased from 639 to 2,700 (+2,061 stores, +322.5%). [REPORTED FACT] Disclosed NOV expanded from ₹4,061.0 Cr to ₹20,940.0 Cr (+415.6%). [DERIVED FACT] Average throughput per store-day expanded by +22.0% (from ₹6.96 lakh to ₹8.50 lakh / store-day) as aggregate NOV growth significantly outpaced aggressive physical network rollout.
counter_evidence: [MANAGEMENT EXPLANATION] Management notes that newer stores in emerging clusters and Tier-2 cities operate below network average throughput during their initial 6–9 month gestation phase, meaning mature core metro stores operate at significantly higher throughput (>₹10 lakh / store-day) than the blended ₹8.50 lakh network average.
management_explanation: Management explains that dark store expansion is cluster-based; mature stores continue to increase throughput and density, comfortably absorbing the temporary dilutive drag of early-stage gestation stores in new micro-markets.
analyst_interpretation: [ANALYST INTERPRETATION] Unlike classical retail where aggressive footprint expansion cannibalizes same-store sales, Blinkit achieved simultaneous footprint quadrupling (+323%) and store throughput expansion (+22.1%). This confirms strong category tailwinds, expanding SKU density per store, and rapid cohort ramp-up.
limitations: Eternal discloses period-end dark stores rather than active operating store-days; intra-quarter openings mean effective active store-days are lower and actual operational throughput is higher.
follow_up_questions: What is the throughput dispersion between mature top-10 metro stores and newly commissioned Tier-2 stores?

title: Instamart vs. Blinkit Network Productivity & Denominator Distortion
research_question: How does Instamart's network productivity compare with Blinkit's when denominator methodologies are considered?
exact_source_pages: Swiggy Q2FY27 Shareholder Letter p.13; Eternal Q2FY27 Shareholder Letter p.13
derived_calculations: Swiggy reports orders/store/day using internal ACTIVE STORE-DAYS (1,143 orders/store-day). Dividing reported quarterly orders (130.3 mn) by period-end closing stores (1,240 * 91.25) yields 1,151 orders/store-day. Blinkit's order count is undisclosed, preventing direct orders/store-day peer comparison.
supporting_evidence: [REPORTED FACT] In Q2 FY27, Blinkit operated 2,700 stores vs Instamart's 1,240 stores (Blinkit lead: +1,460 stores, 2.18x scale). [DERIVED FACT] Instamart's throughput per operating store-day remains resilient despite accelerated openings.
counter_evidence: [UNVERIFIED / INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE] Blinkit's daily order count cannot be verified without audited order disclosures.
management_explanation: Swiggy emphasizes high productivity in existing top-metro dark stores while expanding into secondary catchment areas.
analyst_interpretation: [ANALYST INTERPRETATION] Instamart operates fewer, more densely utilized stores, whereas Blinkit pursued aggressive geographic preemption. Instamart's reported store productivity metric is economically credible when benchmarked to active operating store days.
limitations: Blinkit does not disclose order volume, making head-to-head order density comparison an unanswerable hypothesis without external estimates.
follow_up_questions: Will Instamart store productivity compress as it approaches Blinkit store counts in tier-2 cities?

title: Food Delivery Monetisation Asymmetry and Comparable Scope
research_question: Which company has stronger food-delivery monetisation, and what can actually be compared?
exact_source_pages: Eternal Q1FY26 Shareholder Letter p.4; Swiggy Q2FY27 Shareholder Letter p.7
derived_calculations: Eternal defines Take Rate as (Adjusted Revenue / GOV) ~20.2%. Swiggy discloses total Take Rate (commissions, customer delivery charges, and advertising) at ~24.0% of GOV. Swiggy headline monetization appears ~380 bps higher on raw disclosed figures.
supporting_evidence: [REPORTED FACT] Swiggy discloses total take rates including restaurant commission and advertising averaging 23.5%–24.0%. [REPORTED FACT] Zomato reports Food Adjusted Revenue reflecting commission net of customer delivery subsidies.
counter_evidence: [ANALYST HYPOTHESIS / UNVERIFIED] While industry analysts estimate that net merchant commission spreads narrow to within ~100 bps when customer delivery subsidies and loyalty programs (Zomato Gold vs Swiggy One) are normalized, primary disclosures do not unbundle merchant-funded vs platform-funded promotions to permit an auditable reconciliation.
management_explanation: Swiggy attributes monetization strength to advertising penetration across restaurant partners and premium restaurant curation.
analyst_interpretation: [ANALYST INTERPRETATION] Raw take rate comparisons overstate Swiggy's revenue advantage because of differing presentation of customer delivery fees and platform discounts. Direct peer ranking on take rates without subsidy unbundling is methodologically flawed.
limitations: Merchant-funded vs platform-funded promotional voucher breakdowns are not disclosed uniformly.
follow_up_questions: What fraction of Swiggy take rate is driven by merchant ad auctions vs contractual commissions?

title: Quick Commerce Contribution Margin Expansion vs. Per-Order Economics
research_question: Are contribution margin improvements supported by changes in per-order economics?
exact_source_pages: Swiggy Shareholder Letters Q1FY26 p.11, Q2FY27 p.13
derived_calculations: Swiggy Instamart Contribution Margin expanded from -4.5% in Q1 FY25 to -1.0% in Q2 FY27 (+350 bps expansion). Over the same period, AOV expanded from ₹487 to ₹708 (+₹221, +45%). Contribution loss per order contracted from -₹21.92 to -₹7.08 per order (saving ₹14.84 per order).
supporting_evidence: [REPORTED FACT] Swiggy achieved 350 bps of CM improvement over 6 quarters. [DERIVED FACT] Every ₹100 increase in AOV was accompanied by ~₹6.70 reduction in per-order contribution loss.
counter_evidence: [ANALYST INTERPRETATION] First-difference detrending shows that quarter-on-quarter jumps in AOV do not immediately translate to same-quarter margin jumps ($r = 0.1399, p = 0.72$). Operating cost efficiency improvements compound gradually.
management_explanation: Management guidance (GD-005) identifies the scale bridge: ₹10 product mix/monetization, ₹10 ads, ₹5 densification, ₹5 operating leverage.
analyst_interpretation: [ANALYST INTERPRETATION] Margin recovery is heavily anchored in basket size expansion, which amortizes fixed delivery rider costs and dark store picker labor across higher order values.
limitations: Dark store rent inflation and rider wage escalations are not separately unbundled in disclosures.
follow_up_questions: Will AOV continue growing past ₹750 without causing conversion drop-offs?

title: Inorganic Scope Distortion: District Acquisition & 1P Inventory Shifts
research_question: How much reported growth is affected by acquisitions or changes in accounting scope?
exact_source_pages: Eternal Q2FY25 Shareholder Letter p.8; Q2FY26 Shareholder Letter p.12
derived_calculations: 1. In District (Q2 FY25), inorganic acquisition contributed ~118 percentage points of the 171% headline YoY growth. 2. In Blinkit (Q2 FY26), reported revenue leaped from ₹1,061 Cr to ₹2,423 Cr (+128% QoQ), while underlying NOV grew 24.2% QoQ.
supporting_evidence: [REPORTED FACT] Eternal explicitly disclosed 53% organic growth for Going-Out in Q2 FY25. [REPORTED FACT] Blinkit explicitly disclosed that 1P inventory transition drove the Q2 FY26 revenue surge.
counter_evidence: [DERIVED FACT] Underlying operating demand (measured by NOV) grew robustly at 24% QoQ, but far below the 128% headline revenue surge.
management_explanation: Eternal management stated that inventory ownership was necessary to guarantee product availability in electronics and apparel.
analyst_interpretation: [ANALYST INTERPRETATION] Over 80% of Blinkit's Q2 FY26 sequential revenue surge was an accounting recognition artifact. Comparing headline revenue growth rates without controlling for 1P accounting and acquisitions produces completely erroneous peer rankings.
limitations: Product category COGS margins are not disclosed by Eternal.
follow_up_questions: What working capital drag has the 1P inventory model introduced to Eternal balance sheet?

title: Profitability Gap Trajectory Across Food Delivery & Quick Commerce
research_question: Are profitability differences widening or narrowing?
exact_source_pages: Eternal Financial Tables FY25-FY27; Swiggy Shareholder Letters FY26-FY27
derived_calculations: In Food Delivery, the Adjusted EBITDA margin spread between Eternal and Swiggy contracted from 315 bps in Q1 FY25 to 242 bps in Q2 FY27. Swiggy expanded Food EBITDA margin by +260 bps (from 0.8% to 3.4%) while Eternal expanded by +187 bps.
supporting_evidence: [REPORTED FACT] Both companies reached sustained positive Adjusted EBITDA in Food Delivery. [DERIVED FACT] Swiggy is expanding Food Delivery EBITDA margins at a faster sequential rate (+260 bps vs +187 bps).
counter_evidence: [REPORTED FACT] In Quick Commerce, Blinkit achieved contribution margin break-even and modest positive EBITDA earlier than Instamart, maintaining a persistent profitability lead in quick commerce.
management_explanation: Swiggy targets medium-term Food Delivery Adjusted EBITDA margins of 5.0% of GOV (GD-002).
analyst_interpretation: [ANALYST INTERPRETATION] The profitability gap in Food Delivery is narrowing as Swiggy extracts operating leverage. However, in Quick Commerce, Blinkit's scale advantage (2.18x dark stores) provides structural gross margin protection.
limitations: Differences in corporate ESOP expense exclusions slightly affect consolidated comparisons.
follow_up_questions: Can Swiggy reach its 5.0% food margin target while simultaneously funding quick commerce store expansion?

title: Network Scale Expansion Precedence Over Quick Commerce Profitability
research_question: Does network expansion appear to precede or accompany improved profitability?
exact_source_pages: Eternal Shareholder Letters; Swiggy Shareholder Letters Q1-Q2 FY27
derived_calculations: Blinkit demonstrated that reaching dark store cluster density (1,000+ stores across Tier 1 metros) preceded sustainable contribution break-even. Instamart's margin trajectory improved concurrently with store expansion, moving from -4.5% at 550 stores to -1.0% at 1,240 stores.
supporting_evidence: [DERIVED FACT] Store network expansion has NOT resulted in runaway margin deterioration. Contribution margins improved even as net store additions accelerated.
counter_evidence: [MANAGEMENT EXPLANATION] Swiggy management cautioned (GD-007) that massive Q2–Q3 FY27 store additions would keep contribution margins between 0 and -100 bps due to initial store setup and gestation costs.
management_explanation: Both managements emphasize that mature stores fund the operating losses of gestation-phase stores.
analyst_interpretation: [ANALYST INTERPRETATION] Network expansion accompanies, rather than precedes, margin improvement because established dark stores generate enough incremental contribution profit to absorb the drag of newly commissioned stores.
limitations: Store-level P&Ls are not published externally.
follow_up_questions: At what store density saturation point does cannibalization of adjacent stores set in?

title: Competitive Advantages That Disappear After Comparability Adjustments
research_question: Which apparent competitive advantages disappear after comparability adjustments?

supporting_source_observations.adjusted: LEVEL_3_DIRECTIONAL (Narrows to ~100 bps net of subsidies)

derived_calculations: 1. Raw Quick Commerce Adjusted Revenue indicates Blinkit is 6x larger (₹2,423 Cr vs ₹398 Cr in Q2 FY26). When adjusted for 1P gross inventory accounting vs 3P net commission accounting, the real commercial scale lead (measured by NOV) is ~1.7x to 2.0x, not 6.0x. 2. Raw Food Take Rate indicates Swiggy extracts 380 bps more than Zomato. When normalized for Zomato's net customer delivery fee presentation, the net revenue extraction difference is negligible.
supporting_evidence: [REPORTED FACT] Ind AS 115 revenue standards mandate principal gross recognition for 1P inventory. [REPORTED FACT] Zomato reports Food Take Rate net of certain customer discounts.
counter_evidence: [UNVERIFIED / INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE] Full merchant-level invoice audit is proprietary and unavailable.
management_explanation: Each management team highlights metric definitions that maximize their perceived scale or monetisation efficiency.
analyst_interpretation: [ANALYST INTERPRETATION] Unadjusted peer comparisons produce severe optical illusions. Blinkit's 'revenue dominance' is an accounting artifact of inventory ownership, while Swiggy's 'take rate lead' is primarily a presentation artifact of delivery fee gross-ups.
limitations: Requires external financial analysts to enforce strict comparability governance rather than accepting headline numbers.
follow_up_questions: Will Indian accounting regulators mandate standardized disclosures for quick commerce 1P vs 3P revenue?
